messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: metering-invoice-sync-delay (PD-8231) — Impact: usage ingestion delay for billing pipeline. Severity: P1. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-8231
maya: ack — I'm on call. tagging @sam @lee. quick status: any customer-facing impact yet?
sam: looking now. checking kafka consumer lag, consumer offsets, and ingest-worker pod health.
lee: billing dashboards show missing token counts for the last ~2 hours. Top-10 customers show ~8k tokens missing overall. potential invoice undercount risk.
jordan: adding context — we've seen similar when checkpoint commits stall (last time was a corrupt S3 checkpoint). i'll check checkpoint writer logs.
sam: consumer group metering-ingest lag = 1.9M messages, last commit ~2h ago. ingest-worker-7 shows CrashLoopBackOff, reason OOMKilled in kube events.
maya: any deploys in the last 3 hours that touched ingestion?
sam: yes — deploy of metering-ingest v2.3.4 at 12:03 UTC (rolling). rollout shows some pods on v2.3.4, some still on v2.3.3.
lee: flagged customers: corp-acme, green-health, blue-retail (tickets pending). recommend setting invoice hold until we reconcile.
maya: plan: 1) prevent invoice auto-close (lee) 2) scale ingest workers & restart stuck pods (sam) 3) run backfill for 2h window (jordan) 4) monitor and update PD notes.
lee: done — set invoice_hold=true for impacted accounts, notified finance and CS. ticket #12345 opened.
sam: scaling ingest-workers from 10 -> 30 now:
sam: ```
kubectl scale deployment/metering-ingest --replicas=30 -n prod
kubectl get pods -l app=metering-ingest -n prod
```
sam: restarted CrashLoop pods (kubectl rollout restart deploy/metering-ingest). watching logs: consumer rebalanced and resumed processing offsets. offsets moving: 1.9M -> 250k in last 6m.
jordan: kicked off backfill job backfill-1945678901-2h-window (target window 2024-11-05T10:00:00Z -> 2024-11-05T12:00:00Z). estimated time to catch up: ~45m.
incident-bot: PD note appended: acknowledged by maya. escalation policy still in place. PD link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-8231/notes
sam: quick root-cause hypothesis: v2.3.4 introduced a change in the S3 checkpointing library -> increased memory use -> occasional OOM -> consumer stall. reverting or patching memory usage needed.
lee: customer comms prepared. posting from support: "We're seeing a delay in usage reporting; invoices may be adjusted after reconciliation. We're holding invoice generation for impacted accounts."
maya: monitoring target: ingestion lag < 10k msgs within 60m. adding dashboard alert to slack channel.
jordan: backfill progress: 30% done after 12m, throughput ~120k msgs/min, ETA to catch up ~38m. logs show steady consumption.
alex: (oncall followup) will accept handoff in 40m. pls leave current checkpoint for next oncall and update PD before handoff.
maya: planning handoff notes: status = backfill running (30%), invoice_hold=true for impacted customers, finance notified, postmortem owner = sam. expected full reconciliation in ~2h.
alex: ack — i'll take over at handoff. ping me if throughput drops below 50k msg/min.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-8231 acknowledged by maya at 1945678915.
maya: quick summary for the log: cause = memory regression after v2.3.4 -> OOMs on ingest-worker -> consumer group lag -> invoice undercount risk. mitigation = scale + restart + backfill, invoice holds applied. next steps = revert or patch v2.3.4, postmortem, reconcile invoices.
sam: creating rollback/patch PR now (link: https://git.example/r/redwood/metering/pulls/1428). will coordinate rollback if backfill doesn't finish within 2h.
jordan: backfill complete at ~1945681980, final lag < 5k, running final validation checks against billing counts.
lee: validation shows token counts reconciled for impacted window, will clear invoice_hold after confirmation from finance.
maya: closing notes: incident mitigated, PD-8231 will be resolved after finance sign-off. postmortem assigned to sam. handing off to alex for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
pagerduty-bot: PD-8231 status -> Monitoring (acknowledged).
